title: Why vague aspirations make bad goals: set specific, deliverable goals as a developer
summary: Theo argues that aspirations like "be an engineer," "learn React," or "contribute to open source" are not goals because they have no clear end. Break them down into concrete deliverables you build, tied to problems you care about, and let the aspirations follow. Passion feeds you through the hard parts, and even failed goals make you a better engineer.

principles.text: Aspirations are not goals. Goals need a clear, deliverable end so you know when you've succeeded.
principles.quote: engineers treat aspirations like goals aspirations are not goals aspirations are not a thing you should be working towards goals are the things you should be working towards and goals should have deliverable ends

principles.text: Keep asking questions of a vague aspiration until it becomes a specific thing you can build.
principles.quote: take that top level imaginary goal of i want to learn react and ask yourself more questions until you get to a deliverable thing

principles.text: Build things to learn. Pick projects around problems you personally have, such as a calculator for a game you play.
principles.quote: building goals around specific problems you can solve will make delivering on them significantly easier

principles.text: Don't start from the goal of contributing to open source. Use a project you already care about and contribute when you hit a real problem.
principles.quote: if you start from a point of genuine interest in the project and then contribute it's going to go a lot better than starting with the goal of contributing and then picking a project

principles.text: Pick destinations you're excited about and proud of, so the pain of getting there is worth it and reinforces the result.
principles.quote: the journey sucks way harder if you don't like the destination so pick destinations you're excited about and proud of

principles.text: Detours and abandoned goals still make you a better engineer, and how you talk about failure is a strong hiring signal.
principles.quote: one of the biggest signals i have for a successful engineer is not how many huge things they've built successfully it's how they handle failure
